# bwebs <picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="man/figures/logo-dark.png"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="bwebs logo" /></picture>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/STABLE-uv/bwebs/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/STABLE-uv/bwebs/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

bwebs builds food webs for the samples of a community (taxa with abundances
or biomasses in sites and dates) from compilations of published trophic
interactions, and quantifies how uncertain those webs are. It infers the
potential links among the taxa with the WebBuilder logic of Gray et al.
(2015), estimates with a Bayesian hierarchical model how often links inferred
with each kind of taxonomic evidence are observed in independent food webs,
gives the pairs without an inferred link a small probability that decays
with the taxonomic distance to the nearest recorded interaction, lowers the
probability of predation between taxa of implausible body sizes when their
masses are known, samples plausible webs from those probabilities and
summarises their
topological indicators (connectance, trophic levels, omnivory, trophic
similarity, robustness...) with credible intervals, for every sample and for
contrasts between groups of samples. The matching rule and the way of
combining sources used by default were chosen among 21 rules and several
sources (the Gray et al. registry, Global Biotic Interactions, the
freshwater food webs of GATEWAy and their combinations) by cross-validated
Brier scores, and tested on an independent food web (Tuesday Lake).

It ships the registry of 20,822 freshwater trophic interactions of Gray et
al. (2015) (CC0) and the 19,185 links of the 81 freshwater food webs of
GATEWAy version 1.0 ([Brose et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-019-0899-x),
CC BY 4.0), the calibrations of the Gray
registry alone, combined with GATEWAy and combined with GloBI, the
effect of body size on predation fitted to the aquatic webs of GATEWAy, the
Tuesday Lake food webs of 1984 and 1986 (from the cheddar package), and
downloads interactions from Global Biotic Interactions (GloBI).

## Installation

From GitHub, with its dependencies and the vignette:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("STABLE-uv/bwebs", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

bwebs needs R (>= 3.6.0) and the packages MASS, stats, utils and withr;
igraph is needed only for modularity.

## Example

The example community is invented: 23 freshwater taxa in three control and
three exposed samples.

```{r example}
library(bwebs)

# 1. Nodes and their matching ladder
nodes <- prepare_nodes(example_taxa)

# 2. Metaweb of potential links, with the evidence of each link, from the
#    bundled registries of Gray et al. (2015) and GATEWAy
mw <- build_metaweb(nodes, combine_registries(gray2015, gateway))
mw

# 3. Calibration of those registries (bundled; refit with calibrate_links())
gray2015_gateway_calibration

# 4. Probability of every resource -> consumer pair: the inferred links by
#    their class of evidence, the other pairs by the taxonomic decay
P <- link_probabilities(mw, gray2015_gateway_calibration)
round(P[c("cocconeis_placentula", "cpom", "baetis_rhodani", "simulium"),
        c("gammarus_pulex", "cordulegaster_boltonii")], 2)

# 5. Plausible metawebs drawn from those probabilities and the indicators of
#    every sample in every draw
draws <- sample_metawebs(mw, gray2015_gateway_calibration, n_draws = 100, seed = 2026)
ind <- calc_indicators(draws, example_community, permanent = c("cpom", "fpom"))

# In draws with very few links a sample can be left without links: its
# indicators are undefined (status "empty_web")
table(ind$values$status)

# 6. Posterior summaries by treatment, and contrasts within draws; na_rm = TRUE
#    leaves out the draws where an indicator is undefined (see n_missing)
summarize_indicators(ind, indicators = c("S", "C", "TL_mean"), samples = example_samples,
                     by = "treatment", na_rm = TRUE)[, c(1:7, 13)]
contrast_indicators(ind, example_samples, by = "treatment", reference = "control",
                    indicators = c("S", "C", "TL_mean"), na_rm = TRUE)[, c(1, 3:8, 10)]
```

## Methods and decisions

* **Matching rule** (`matching_rule()`): every node is matched with the
  registry at family level and climbs to order and class until it links with
  at least five other nodes; every registry is used at every level; predators
  do not climb as resources; records resolved only to a coarse rank and
  generic resources ("Algae") are extended downwards; surrogates and manual
  links are explicit decisions of the user.
* **Choice of the rule and the sources** (`candidate_rules()`,
  `compare_rules()`): 21 rules (fixed matching, climbing and the WebBuilder
  ladder of Gray et al. 2015, from several starting levels and thresholds)
  were scored on the 12 validation webs of the registry other than Tuesday
  Lake, each rebuilt without the studies of its system
  (`gray2015_rule_comparison`); the main eight were scored again with GloBI
  records and with both sources, leaving out of each web the GloBI studies
  that copy it (`source_comparison`). The default, climbing from family to
  class with both sources at every level, had the lowest mean Brier score
  (0.199, against 0.223 with the Gray registry alone): GloBI raised the share
  of recorded links that are inferred from 67% to 91% with the same
  precision (39%). Climbing from family scored better than starting at genus,
  the ladder or no generalisation with every source; the threshold (one or
  five partners) made no difference larger than its standard error. The
  result held without the secondary compilations of GloBI (metawebs and
  trait databases). With the decay, the freshwater webs of GATEWAy lowered
  the score of the Gray registry from 0.209 to 0.205 but raised that of
  Gray + GloBI from 0.197 to 0.201: Gray + GloBI is the best combination,
  and Gray + GATEWAy the best one that can be distributed
  (`gray2015_gateway_calibration`, used in the examples).
* **Class of evidence** (`build_metaweb()`): the taxonomic generalisation
  needed by the best record that supports each link (same taxon, genus,
  subfamily, family, order, class, generic group). Each link also keeps how
  much evidence supports it: its records and studies, and the relatives of
  the consumer and of the resource among them.
* **Calibration** (`validate_rule()`, `calibrate_links()`): a logistic model
  with one coefficient per class of evidence and a random effect of the web,
  fitted to how many inferred links were observed in the webs left out, with
  weakly informative priors and a posterior sampled by Metropolis-Hastings.
  The classes are ordered (since 0.3.0): a link supported by a closer
  relative is never less probable than one supported by a more distant
  relative; free coefficients, which broke that order, scored the same in
  the cross-validation. The probability of a link is that of observing it
  in a comparable well-studied community, a lower bound for its existence.
  It depends on the class only: the amount of evidence of a link (studies,
  records, supporting relatives, or the shares of the relatives that
  support it) did not improve the predictions for the webs left out with
  any of the registries compared, and its effect changed sign from one
  registry to another.
* **Taxonomic decay** (`matching_rule(decay = TRUE)`, the default since
  0.3.0): the pairs without an inferred link take a probability from a
  second model of the same form, by how close the registry comes to them:
  the closest level at which relatives of the consumer have recorded diets
  and the closest level at which the resource is related to that diet, never
  lower for closer evidence, and the size of the web (connectance usually
  falls as webs grow). In the cross-validation it lowered the Brier score
  from 0.1988 to 0.1971 with Gray + GloBI and from 0.223 to 0.209 with the
  Gray registry; on Tuesday Lake it improved every score.
* **Body masses** (`sample_metawebs(masses = )`): the probability of a
  predation pair is lowered by how far the predator/prey mass ratio is from
  the optimum, a within-consumer effect fitted to the 206 aquatic webs of
  GATEWAy (`size_model`; a flat curve with its optimum at a consumer about
  17,000 times heavier than its prey), with weights for the inferred links
  (0.25) and for the pairs of the decay (1). The curve, its webs and the
  weights were chosen by the validation by folds of the 12 validation webs
  with body masses: their mean Brier score went down by 0.006 (9 of 12 webs
  better), and that of Tuesday Lake from 0.140 to 0.137 with Gray + GloBI
  and from 0.149 to 0.139 with Gray + GATEWAy. The masses can change from
  draw to draw (the draws of a biomass model), so that each sampled web
  holds its links and the masses of its taxa from the same draw.
* **Sampling** (`sample_metawebs()`): in each draw the parameters come from
  the posterior and, by default, the effect of the system from its
  distribution (an unknown system); each link is kept with the probability of
  its class, and each pair without a link with that of its evidence, both
  shifted by the size term when the masses are given. `link_probabilities()`
  gives the matrix of those probabilities, averaged over the posterior and
  the effect of the system: a pair of probability 0.25 is present in about
  one draw in four. The same draw is used
  for every sample, so contrasts between samples are computed within draws
  (`contrast_indicators()`).
* **Independent test** (`score_metaweb()`, `tuesday_lake_taxa`): with
  registries and calibrations without Tuesday Lake, the default rule
  inferred 71% of the links of the Tuesday Lake webs (22% with the Gray
  registry alone, which has few diets of plankton). The ranking of the
  combinations on Tuesday Lake agreed with the cross-validation (Spearman
  0.73). With the decay and the ordered classes, the Brier skill over the
  null model was 0.19 with Gray + GloBI (0.13 with Gray alone, 0.16 with
  Gray + GATEWAy), and among taxa the sampled webs came close to the
  observed ones in connectance, mean trophic level and proportion of top
  taxa; with the body masses of Tuesday Lake as well, 0.20 (0.14 with Gray,
  0.21 with Gray + GATEWAy).
* **Indicators** (`web_indicators()`): on the web without cannibalism and
  without isolated nodes, aggregated into trophic species.

Decisions to make for each data set: which studies are used for the
calibration (`validate_rule(sources = )`) and which of them describe the
same system (`groups = `; see `shared_studies()`), whether the system is
unknown or typical (`sample_metawebs(system = )`), and which unsampled
resources are always present (`calc_indicators(permanent = )`). See the
vignette (`vignette("bwebs")`) and the help pages.

## Status

Version 0.3.0, experimental and not on CRAN.

* The metaweb engine and the indicators reproduce exactly the code of the
  original analysis (1319 links of a 108-node metaweb; 27 indicators of 120
  webs) with the rule of that analysis (`matching_rule(min_partners = 1)`).
* The maximum-likelihood fit agrees with `lme4::glmer(nAGQ = 20)`; the
  Bayesian fit agrees with the posterior computed on a grid for a small
  problem.
* Indicators are checked against hand calculations and igraph.
* `R CMD check --as-cran` runs without errors and with all tests passing
  on Ubuntu 24.04 with R 4.3.3; GitHub Actions runs `R CMD check` on macOS,
  Windows and Ubuntu.
* The GloBI download used for the comparison of sources and for
  `gray2015_globi_calibration` (832,003 records, 3 November 2026) is not
  included; `dev/globi/` has the scripts that download and process it,
  `dev/gateway/` the one that turns GATEWAy into a registry, and
  `dev/validation/` those of the comparisons (results in
  `dev/validation/results.md`).

## Known limitations

* Without body masses the taxonomic decay knows nothing of size: for
  consumers whose relatives have few records it spreads probability over
  pairs that size would exclude (rotifers eating fish), so in the sampled
  webs of Tuesday Lake most consumers were omnivores (in 1984, 0.95 of the
  trophic species with Gray + GATEWAy and 0.84 with Gray + GloBI, against
  0.50 observed; 0.86 and 0.69 with the body masses), and the links it
  adds among consumers form loops that raise the mean trophic level (in the
  example above, which has no masses, from 2.0 without the decay to 2.7,
  with 2.5% of the sampled webs above 5.1). It over-predicts the links among
  the pairs not inferred of the validation webs (in the cross-validation,
  846 expected against 477 recorded with Gray + GloBI, 1,601 against 1,421
  with Gray + GATEWAy), and its draws vary a lot in their number of links
  when the system effect is drawn (`sample_metawebs(system = "random")`).
  `matching_rule(decay = FALSE)` gives the webs of version 0.2.0.
* The size term was validated on the 12 validation webs with body masses
  (streams and ponds) and on Tuesday Lake. Most of the pairs of its curve
  come from marine webs (474,717 of 491,829), and it makes the score of the
  webs whose recorded links are mostly predation worse (Broadstone Stream,
  Skipwith Pond), which is why its weight on the inferred links is small.
* The indicators of trophic species of the observed and sampled webs are
  not comparable: the observed webs collapse into few trophic species
  (many producers share their consumers), the sampled ones do not.
* The probabilities of the classes of evidence come from 13 validation
  webs, mostly of British rivers and streams, and transfer imperfectly to
  other systems: the generic class ("Algae" extended to all algae) was
  calibrated at 0.61 with the Gray registry as the primary registry, but
  only 13% of those links were observed in Tuesday Lake.
* Only studies 13 and 50 are left out together as webs of the same system;
  46 and 49 (Woodward, Hildrew et al.) and 15 and 59 (P. H. Warren) may also
  describe the same systems (`validate_rule(groups = )`).
* The links of GATEWAy were established in different ways (gut contents,
  the literature, expert knowledge), and some of its webs have coarse diets
  (in the Adirondack lakes of Havens 1992, 59% of the predator-prey pairs
  are links): added to Gray + GloBI it made the cross-validation worse. The
  five chalk streams of Gray et al. (2015) and Thompson et al. (2017), built
  partly with WebBuilder from the Gray registry, are left out of `gateway`
  but are in the GloBI download; without them the cross-validation of Gray
  + GloBI was worse, perhaps in part because they carry information of the
  validation webs.
* `gray2015_globi_calibration` was fitted with the GloBI records downloaded
  for the consumers of the validation webs, of Tuesday Lake and of the
  azoxystrobin experiment of Amador et al. (2024); a metaweb built with
  another GloBI download is only approximately calibrated by it.
* The threshold of five partners was chosen by a margin smaller than its
  standard error; `matching_rule(min_partners = 1)` gives the rule of the
  original analysis.
